content.text:
The January data (the only same-season comparison available since the series is Jan 2018 – Dec 2018 then Jan 2019) shows F3_Z01 at 23.86 → 24.57 (+0.7), but peer F1_Z01 rose 25.08 → 27.13 (+2.0) while F3_Z02, F3_Z03, F3_Z05, and F4_Z01 all *declined*. The VAV_F3_Z01 damper setpoint barely moves (+0.02). So the signal isn't cleanly isolable:

- The rise in F3_Z01 is smaller than the rise in some other zones (F1_Z01), so it's plausibly a building-wide effect rather than zone-local.
- Peer-zone sensors on the same (F3) floor all moved the *other way*, suggesting F3_Z01 may have drifted high — but a sensor fault is also entirely consistent with a local load/occupancy change affecting only F3_Z01.
- The controller's thermostat is explicitly not in the data, so we can't confirm the *true* air temperature moved, only the reported value.

The two candidate causes (local load change vs. sensor fault in the monitoring sensor) cannot be separated from the available streams.

input.needed_streams: Independent zone air temperature sensor for the same Core_mid zone (Zone_F3_Z01) separate from the reporting monitoring sensor, plus the zone's controller thermostat / actual zone-air temperature signal used by the VAV controller, and outdoor ambient dry-bulb temperature (or a reference zone with no expected load change) for seasonal normalisation. The available streams (single monitoring ZoneAirTemperatureSensor for F3_Z01, peer zone sensors on the same floor, VAV_F3_Z01 damper position setpoint, and zone heating/cooling setpoints) only show the reported F3_Z01 value trending ~+0.7 °C above early-2018 levels while some other zones also moved and F3 Z02/Z03/Z05 and F4_Z01 moved the opposite direction — this is ambiguous between a real local load change in F3_Z01 and a bias/drift in the F3_Z01 monitoring sensor, and cannot be disambiguated without an independent co-located temperature reading and the controller's own temperature reference.
